name: Radiation dose
question: Effective dose in sieverts (Sv). Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Eating a banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium-40.

items.name: Airport security scan (US limit)
items.fact: Airport scanner limits are a fraction of a single day's natural background dose.

items.name: Dental X-rays
items.fact: A set of dental X-rays is about the same as a day of natural background radiation.

items.name: Chest X-ray
items.fact: A chest X-ray gives about the dose of a long-haul flight.

items.name: A year as a flight attendant
items.fact: At cruising altitude there's less atmosphere shielding you from cosmic rays.

items.name: A year of natural background radiation
items.fact: Radon gas seeping from the ground is the largest single source of natural background radiation.

items.name: Full-body CT scan
items.fact: A full-body CT scan equals several years of natural background radiation.

items.name: Yearly limit for US radiation workers
items.fact: Limits for workers are set well below doses that cause any visible harm.

items.name: Six months on the Space Station
items.fact: Astronauts get about 80 mSv in six months on the ISS.

items.name: A year of smoking 1.5 packs a day (lungs)
items.fact: Tobacco contains radioactive polonium-210 and lead-210.

items.name: Six-month trip to Mars
items.fact: Cosmic rays are very hard to shield against on the way to Mars.

items.name: NASA astronaut career limit
items.fact: NASA caps astronauts at 1 sievert over their whole career.

items.name: Dose fatal to half of people (short exposure)
items.fact: Doses spread out over time are far less harmful than the same dose all at once.
